MB1.code:
from xmd_quantum import FockBasis
basis = FockBasis(n_orbitals=4, particle_number=2)

MB2.title: Reduce an active model space
MB2.summary: Apply an occupation restriction and compare the reduced Hilbert-space size with the unrestricted basis
MB2.code:
from xmd_quantum import FockBasis, OccupationRestriction
full = FockBasis(6, 2)
restricted = FockBasis(6, 2, restrictions=(
    OccupationRestriction(orbitals=(0,1,2), min_particles=1, max_particles=2),
))
print("full:", full.dimension, "restricted:", restricted.dimension)

MB3.title: Build a two-site hopping Hamiltonian
MB3.summary: Compose fermionic operators into a minimal hopping Hamiltonian and solve it
MB3.code:
from xmd_quantum import FockBasis, FermionOperator, dense_eigensystem
basis = FockBasis(2, 1)
c, cdag, n = FermionOperator.annihilation, FermionOperator.creation, FermionOperator.number
H = -(cdag(0)*c(1) + cdag(1)*c(0)) + 0.5*n(1)
solution = dense_eigensystem(H.to_sparse(basis))
print(solution.energies)

MB4.title: Inspect a ground-state wavefunction
MB4.summary: Extract the lowest eigenvector and evaluate one orbital occupation
MB4.code:
import numpy as np
from xmd_quantum import FockBasis, FermionOperator, dense_eigensystem
basis = FockBasis(2, 1)
c, cdag = FermionOperator.annihilation, FermionOperator.creation
H = -(cdag(0)*c(1) + cdag(1)*c(0))
solution = dense_eigensystem(H.to_sparse(basis))
psi0 = solution.vectors[:, 0]
n1 = FermionOperator.number(1).to_sparse(basis)
print("orbital-1 occupation:", np.vdot(psi0, n1 @ psi0).real)

MB5.title: Verify particle number in a fixed-N sector
MB5.summary: Convert a composed operator to a sparse matrix and verify total particle number
MB5.code:
import numpy as np
from xmd_quantum import FockBasis, FermionOperator
basis = FockBasis(4, 2)
N = sum((FermionOperator.number(i) for i in range(4)), FermionOperator.zero())
np.testing.assert_allclose(N.to_sparse(basis).toarray(), 2*np.eye(basis.dimension))
print("particle-number check passed")

P2.title: Compare Coulomb screening assumptions
P2.summary: Compare isotropic spectra for two Slater-reduction factors
P2.code:
import numpy as np
from xmd_quantum import run_atomic_2p3d
def xas(reduction):
    r=run_atomic_2p3d(d_electrons=8,f2dd=8.0,f4dd=5.0,f2pd=5.5,g1pd=4.0,g3pd=2.4,zeta_p=8.0,reduction=reduction,points=301)
    return {c.key:c for c in r.channels}["xas-isotropic"]
a,b=xas(1.0),xas(.8)
print(np.max(np.abs(a.intensity-b.intensity)))

P6.title: Check circular-polarization conventions
P6.summary: Verify that right-minus-left absorption matches the XMCD difference channel
P6.code:
import numpy as np
from xmd_quantum import run_atomic_2p3d
r=run_atomic_2p3d(d_electrons=8,zeta_p=8.0,exchange_z=.03,points=301)
ch={c.key:c for c in r.channels}
np.testing.assert_allclose(ch["xas-r"].intensity-ch["xas-l"].intensity,ch["xmcd-r-minus-l"].intensity)
print("helicity convention check passed")

from xmd_quantum import CalculationRequest, run_calculation
request=CalculationRequest("atomic-2p3d",{"d_electrons":8,"zeta_p":8.0,"temperature_K":300.0,"points":301})

R3.title: Round-trip a calculation through JSON
R3.summary: Serialize a request/result and restore the result exactly
R3.code:
from xmd_quantum import CalculationRequest, CalculationResult, run_calculation
request=CalculationRequest("atomic-2p3d",{"d_electrons":0,"points":301})
request_json=request.to_json()
result=run_calculation(request)
restored=CalculationResult.from_json(result.to_json())
assert restored.to_dict()==result.to_dict()
print("JSON round-trip passed")
